hints.content:
##The plan

We can find the area of each trapezoid by multiplying its width by the average of the values of $f(x)$ at the left and right endpoints.

![A trapezoid whose bases are vertical has width b minus a. The left, shorter base has height f of a. The right, taller base has height f of b.](web+graphie:${☣ LOCALPATH}/images/e2a5fa8a5479bf6d93a5f89670f35578f1dc0fad) 

$\text{area of trapezoid}=(b-a)\left( \dfrac{f(a)+f(b)}{2} \right)$

Then we *sum* all of the areas.

## Area of the trapezoids

Let's find the area of the first trapezoid:

$\begin{align}
\text{Area}_1 &= (3-0) \cdot \dfrac{f(0)+f(3)}{2} \\\\
&= 3\cdot \dfrac{7}{2} \\\\
&=10.5
\end{align}$

We can repeat the process for the remaining trapezoids.

$\begin{align}
\text{Area}_2 &= (6-3) \cdot  \dfrac{f(3)+f(6)}{2} \\ \\
&= 3\cdot \dfrac{12}{2} \\\\
&=18
\end{align}$

$\begin{align}
\text{Area}_3 &= (9-6) \cdot  \dfrac{f(6)+f(9)}{2} \\ \\
&= 3\cdot \dfrac{18}{2} \\\\
&=27
\end{align}$

options.explanation:
Because there are equal subdivisions, we don't have to subtract to find the width each time.  

$\text{width}=\dfrac{9-0}{3}=3$

Each of the trapezoid areas shares common factors, so we can factor them out and save some calculation steps.

$\begin{align}
&3\cdot \dfrac{f(0)+f(3)}{2}+3\cdot  \dfrac{f(3)+f(6)}{2}+3\cdot  \dfrac{f(6)+f(9)}{2}= \\\\
&\dfrac{3}{2}(f(0)+2\cdot f(3)+ 2 \cdot f(6) + f(9))= \\\\
&55.5 \end{align}$

question.content:
**Approximate the area between the $x$-axis and $f(x)$ from $x = 0$ to $x = 9$ using a *trapezoidal sum* with $3$ equal subdivisions.**

 | |  |||
:-: | - | - | - |
$x$ | $0$ | $3$ | $6$ | $9$ 
$f(x)$ | $2$ | $5$ | $7$ | $11$
